en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.
8. The Question on the Hunter’s Qualities “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that ‘four qualities of a hunter should be adopted’—which are those four qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a hunter is free from drowsiness;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must be free from drowsiness.
This, Great King, is the first quality to be adopted from the hunter.
Furthermore, Great King, the hunter fixes his mind solely upon the deer.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi who is a practitioner of yoga should fix the mind upon the objects of meditation themselves.
This, Great King, is the second quality to be adopted from the hunter.
Furthermore, Great King, the hunter knows the proper time for his work.
In the same way, Great King, a yogin who is a practitioner of yoga should know the proper time for seclusion, thinking: "This is the time for seclusion; this is the time for emerging.
This, Great King, is the third quality that should be adopted from the hunter.
Furthermore, Great King, when a hunter sees a deer, he gives rise to joy, thinking: "I shall catch this one."
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, should take delight in the object of meditation and generate joy, thinking: "I shall attain a further distinction.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality to be adopted from the hunter.
And this, Great King, was said by the Elder Mogharāja:
“Having obtained an object of focus,
a bhikkhu with a resolute mind should generate even greater joy.”
"I shall attain what is higher.
This is the eighth question, concerning the hunter's limb.
